title: Security: a runAs system flow writes identity-assignment rows (sys_user_position, sys_invitation) past the delegated-administration gate
body:
Ruled: 6354966423 · letter B · 2026-10-23T01:05:47Z

Filing gate ①: a measured authorization defect (reproduction withheld from this public card: possible privilege exposure). Filed by `repo:cloud#1` (seat post #6026, session `session_01FSg7JRUiTPo8GrgT38tAWP`) from a local-stack measurement the maintainer's ruling on objectstack-ai/cloud#3149 asked for (item 5, the two 「to verify」 reads). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Acting reader:** the maintainer first (disclosure and severity call; the full reproduction, flows, rows and log lines are on objectstack-ai/cloud#3149, a private repository), then the `domain:services` / security lane at dispatch.

## What is read (code, framework pin `9d13b5fc`)
- A `runAs: 'system'` flow's data context is `{ isSystem: true, … }` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts:270`–`:277`).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:2405`–`:2407` returns `next()` for `isSystem` **before** `delegatedAdminGate.assert(opCtx)` (`:2546`).
- So the ADR-0090 D12 / ADR-0105 D8 checks never run for such writes: the anchor refusal, the org-admin boundary, adminScope containment, the placement and role cap, and the `granted_by` stamp (`delegated-admin-gate.ts`).
- The gate's header says system writes short-circuit by design (seeders and similar). Tenant-authored flows fall into the same bypass.

## What was measured (local stack only; details withheld here)
- A system flow assigned a non-reserved position to another user, including a position bound to a full-access permission set. The row carried no `granted_by`, and the assignment took effect in that user's session. A scheduled system flow did the same with no acting user at all.
- A system flow wrote a `sys_invitation` row straight into the environment. better-auth then treats it as a real invitation, without the invite door's email, placement or role-cap checks.
- The only check that still applied was the row-level refusal of the four reserved identity names (`sys-user-position.object.ts:256`–`:264`).

## Not measured
- Which principals can author or save a `runAs: 'system'` flow on a hosted environment. The measurement authored as a platform admin. Severity depends on this read, and it comes first at dispatch.

## Wanted
- The governed identity-assignment objects (at least `sys_user_position`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_member`) are not writable by tenant-authored system flows past the D12 gate.
  - Either the gate also runs on `isSystem` contexts that originate from authored flow metadata (with the flow's author or owner as the judged principal), or those objects refuse writes from such contexts outright.
  - Platform seeders keep their path.
- A provenance stamp (`granted_by` / the flow) on whatever path remains.

## Acceptance
On a local stack, a tenant-authored `runAs: 'system'` flow that writes `sys_user_position` or `sys_invitation` is refused, or is judged by the D12 gate as its author would be. A platform seeder's write still succeeds.

Dedupe words: runAs system sys_user_position delegated-admin gate bypass; granted_by unstamped system flow; sys_invitation raw write system flow; isSystem short-circuit RBAC assignment.
